title: The Haymarket Affair
claims: Connects the eight-hour movement, May 3 McCormick violence and May 4 meeting on Desplaines north of Randolph.
The account leaves the bomber unidentified.
limitations: An interpretation, not a current route/access source. Casualty totals and some details differ from other accounts; do not silently harmonize.

title: Site of the Haymarket Tragedy
claims: Municipal landmark describes 151–199 N Desplaines and the rally near Crane’s Alley north of Randolph.
limitations: The address is a landmark range, not the footprint of a reviewed visitor arrival.

title: Chicago labor-history sites
claims: Identifies the Mary Brogger meeting-site memorial at 175 N Desplaines, commemorated in 2004.
Separately lists the cemetery monument at 863 Desplaines Avenue, Forest Park.
limitations: Similar street names and subject matter do not identify the same place. Current cemetery access is unverified.

title: Testimony of Thomas Greif, July 19, 1886, volume I pp. 325–335
publisher: Chicago History Museum, Haymarket Affair Digital Collection
claims: Greif testified for the prosecution and was cross-examined. He gave 54 West Lake and a location east of Clinton.
The account describes hall and basement use and the limits of his knowledge.
limitations: Testimony is attributed evidence, not an independently established conspiracy narrative. The old number is not a modern geocode. Current parcel/building continuity remains unresolved.

title: Testimony of Felix V. Bushick, July 16, 1886, volume I pp. 2–18
publisher: Chicago History Museum, Haymarket Affair Digital Collection
claims: Bushick placed Greif’s Hall on the north side of Lake east of Clinton and gave the historical 54 West Lake number.
The testimony separately describes Zepf’s Hall at Lake and Desplaines.
limitations: Witness uncertainty about storey counts remains uncertainty. Neither transcript supplies a modern parcel mapping or surviving-building inspection.

title: Cook County Criminal Court Building and jail, circa 1879, catalogue record
publisher: Chicago History Museum, Haymarket Affair Digital Collection
claims: Catalogue identifies the earlier courthouse/jail with the trial and execution courtyard.
Credits Alexander J. Copelin, accession 1986.0453 / ICHi 00462.
limitations: Catalogue direction says northeast corner, conflicting with the museum’s separate west-side description. Do not infer an exact courtyard point from this text. The historical photograph is not copied.

title: Cook County Criminal Courthouse area caption
publisher: Chicago History Museum / Northwestern University, The Dramas of Haymarket
claims: Describes the 1874 courthouse on Michigan, now Hubbard, at Dearborn.
States the courthouse was demolished in 1892 for a replacement, later called Courthouse Place; the old jail site became a firehouse.
limitations: Do not present the extant building as the 1886 trial courtroom. Narrative calls replacement the 1892 courthouse; city lists built 1893, so retain the construction/completion distinction.

title: Courthouse Place
claims: Identifies 54 W Hubbard, built 1893, architect Otto H. Matz.
The surviving structure’s later trials are distinct from the Haymarket-era building.
limitations: An exterior interpretation anchor, not permission to enter offices or the former jail site.

title: Haymarket Martyr’s Monument
claims: Locates the monument in Forest Home Cemetery, Forest Park, separate from the Chicago meeting site.
Dates dedication to June 23, 1893 and identifies the Pioneer Aid and Support Association.
limitations: Use for monument identity/dedication. Do not repeat every general-history assertion or infer contemporary cemetery access or a transit itinerary.
